security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by bundled Stripe reference code, generated RBI examples, and command snippets in the Sorbet workflow. The skill intent is to create Ruby Sorbet RBI signature files and validate them locally; no prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious execution intent was found. Static review was capped at 400/22364 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 21964 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Bundled full Stripe reference source creates many marketplace security false positives.
remediation.suggestion: Replace large third-party reference trees with smaller curated RBI examples that demonstrate only the needed Sorbet patterns.

remediation.issue: Validation commands in SKILL.md can be mistaken for broad command execution guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that only Sorbet type-checking commands should be run and that application code must not be executed.

content.value_statement: Ruby teams often need type signatures without changing source files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create accurate Sorbet RBI files and validate them with Sorbet.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes Ruby source files to identify classes, modules, methods, constants, attributes, and visibility modifiers.
Generates Sorbet RBI files under an rbi directory with typed sigils and signature stubs.
Adds T::Sig structure and method signatures without modifying the original Ruby source files.
Guides type inference to reduce T.untyped usage in generated signatures.
Runs Sorbet validation commands such as srb tc or bundle exec srb tc when appropriate.
limitations: It cannot guarantee perfect types for highly dynamic Ruby behavior without project context.
It requires Sorbet and project dependencies to be installed for validation.
It should not run application Ruby code while generating signatures.
It may need user clarification for metaprogramming, DSLs, or ambiguous return types.

use_cases.title: Add types to a legacy Ruby library
use_cases.description: Generate RBI files that describe existing classes and methods without editing legacy source files.

use_cases.title: Describe gem or generated APIs
use_cases.description: Create signatures for APIs that Sorbet cannot infer from source code alone.

use_cases.title: Validate type coverage during migration
use_cases.description: Iterate on generated signatures and run Sorbet checks until the RBI files are accepted.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a basic RBI file
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one Ruby file
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate Sorbet RBI signatures for this Ruby file. Place the result in the rbi directory and avoid changing the source file.

prompt_templates.title: Infer safer method types
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve signatures after a first draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the generated RBI file and replace weak or unknown types with more specific Sorbet types based on the Ruby source and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Handle dynamic Ruby APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Ruby class for methods created by metaprogramming, DSLs, or method_missing. Generate RBI signatures that reflect the public API.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and refine with Sorbet
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the appropriate Sorbet type check command, explain each signature error, update the RBI files, and repeat until validation passes.

output_examples.input: A Ruby class with readers, an initializer, and one public method.
output_examples.output: A matching RBI file with typed sigil, T::Sig extension, reader signatures, initializer parameters, and method return type.

output_examples.input: A Rails model that gains methods from a DSL.
output_examples.output: An RBI description of the generated methods, expected parameter types, return types, and class structure.

output_examples.input: A Sorbet validation error for a generated signature.
output_examples.output: A revised signature plan that explains the mismatch and updates the RBI file to satisfy Sorbet.

best_practices: Read the Ruby source and surrounding tests before choosing parameter and return types.
Keep RBI files as signatures and empty stubs only, with no method bodies.
Validate with Sorbet after generation and refine signatures from the reported errors.
anti_patterns: Do not use T.untyped as a default when source context supports a specific type.
Do not modify Ruby source files when the task asks for separate RBI signatures.
Do not run application code to infer types; use static analysis and Sorbet validation instead.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates Sorbet RBI files that describe Ruby APIs with signatures and empty method stubs.

faq.question: Does it change my Ruby source files?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the agent to place signatures in separate files under the rbi directory.

faq.question: Can it type dynamic Ruby methods?
faq.answer: Yes, it guides analysis of DSLs, method_missing, define_method, and other dynamic API patterns.

faq.question: Does it allow T.untyped?
faq.answer: The skill discourages T.untyped and asks the agent to infer more specific types whenever possible.

faq.question: How are generated files checked?
faq.answer: The skill recommends running Sorbet validation with srb tc or bundle exec srb tc.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Ruby developers, Sorbet maintainers, and teams migrating existing Ruby code to static typing can use it.
